hints: Write 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 in binary. What do all of them have in common? And what happens to zero and negative numbers?
A positive power of two has exactly one set bit. Since n & (n − 1) removes the lowest set bit, a power of two becomes 0. Combine that with a check that n > 0.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: While n is even and positive, divide by 2; it is a power of two if you end at 1.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: One bit test: n > 0 and n & (n − 1) == 0.

explain: Sample 32 = 100000 and 31 = 011111; their AND is 0 and 32 > 0, so the answer is true. For 24 = 11000, 23 = 10111, and the AND is 10000 = 16, not 0, so 24 is not a power of two (it has two set bits). The n > 0 check matters: 0 & −1 = 0 would wrongly pass, and −231 has a single set bit in two's complement but is negative.
recognize: 'Is n a power of two?' → exactly one set bit: n > 0 and n & (n − 1) == 0.
javascript: function isDoubling(n) { if (n <= 0) return false; while (n % 2 === 0) n /= 2; return n === 1; }
